content.prompt: Find the shaded area to 2 d.p.

answer.worked:
The two semicircles removed from the ends have the area of one circle of radius $\frac{8}{2}=4$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}A_1&=16\times8\\A_1&=128\ \mathrm{cm}^2\\A_2&=\pi(4)^2\\A_2&=16\pi\ \mathrm{cm}^2\\A_{\text{Total}}&=A_1-A_2\\A_{\text{Total}}&=128-16\pi\\A_{\text{Total}}&\approx77.73\ \mathrm{cm}^2\end{align*}$$

payloads.replacement: The **area** $A$ of a circle is $A=\pi r^2$, where $r$ is the **radius**, the distance from the centre to the circumference.
If the diameter is given, change it to the [[radius|24]] by [[halving|24]] it before calculating.

A **sector** is the region of a circle enclosed by two radii and the arc between them.

The **interior angle** of a sector is the angle between the two radii, measured inside the sector.

The **exterior angle** is the angle between the two radii, measured outside the sector. The interior and exterior angles sum to $360^\circ$.

A **sector** is the region of a circle enclosed by two radii and the arc between them.

The area of a sector is a fraction of the whole circle, where $\theta$ is the interior angle in degrees.

$$A=\underbrace{\dfrac{\overset{\mathclap{\substack{\textstyle\text{interior angle}\\\downarrow}}}{\theta}}{360}}_{\substack{\rule{0pt}{4mm}\textstyle\text{fraction of}\\\textstyle\text{circle}}}\times\underbrace{\pi r^2}_{\substack{\rule{0pt}{4mm}\textstyle\text{area of whole}\\\textstyle\text{circle}}}$$

content.prompt:
A bakery cuts two sector-shaped pieces from round tarts, as shown.

Which piece has the bigger area and by how much? Round the answer to two decimal places.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{A}}&=\frac{50}{360}\times\pi(12)^2\\A_{\text{A}}&=20\pi\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{B}}&=\frac{80}{360}\times\pi(10)^2\\A_{\text{B}}&=\frac{200\pi}{9}\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{B}}-A_{\text{A}}&=\frac{200\pi}{9}-20\pi\\A_{\text{B}}-A_{\text{A}}&=\frac{20\pi}{9}\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{B}}-A_{\text{A}}&\approx6.98\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
Piece B has the bigger area, by $6.98\text{ cm}^2$.
